hyperedges.label: TTS Lip-Sync Evaluation Pipeline
hyperedges.description: End-to-end pipeline for evaluating TTS model lip-sync quality: TTS synthesis produces audio from text+reference → Ditto animation generates talking-face video from portrait+audio → SyncNet evaluation scores SyncC/SyncD confidence and distance metrics. Uses AISHELL-1 test set with 13 speaker portraits.

hyperedges.label: Model-Server Compatibility
hyperedges.description: Compatibility matrix mapping 8 lip-sync models to two GPU servers based on VRAM, CUDA version, and PyTorch constraints. Old server (8×1080 Ti, CUDA 11.4) runs Wav2Lip and MuseTalk. New models require CUDA 12.x and higher VRAM.

hyperedges.label: SyncD Feature Prediction Pipeline
hyperedges.description: Multi-method analysis predicting SyncNet Distance (SyncD) from 52 audio features: Spearman correlation identifies top predictors (mfcc_3_std r=-0.3363), LASSO selects 43 features (R²=0.6028), Random Forest achieves R²=0.9417. Uses 447 scored rows across multiple TTS providers.

hyperedges.label: Wav2Sem Analysis Pipeline (Phase 1)
hyperedges.description: Five-stage Phase 1 pipeline: data assembly → MFA alignment → HuBERT/XLS-R embedding extraction → separability metrics → TFG linkage → report generation

hyperedges.label: Phase 2 Causal Intervention Pipeline
hyperedges.description: Phase 2 causal chain: feature transformations → dose-response → identity control → corrected analysis → stability PGD perturbation. All acoustic mechanisms rejected; G×E co-adaptation and HuBERT stability survive as candidates.

hyperedges.label: TFG Model Comparison Matrix
hyperedges.description: Six-TFG-model comparison using same audio conditions (natural 16kHz vs faster_qwen3 TTS 24kHz) on AISHELL-1 subset, evaluated via SyncNet v2

hyperedges.label: Lip-Sync Model Comparison Pipeline
hyperedges.description: Five lip-sync models deployed across two servers, benchmarked with SyncNet metrics. Wav2Lip ranked best overall; all models show TTS speech improves Sync-C over natural speech.

hyperedges.label: Audio Feature Analysis for Lip-Sync Prediction
hyperedges.description: Multi-figure exploratory analysis of 15+ audio features and their relationship to lip-sync metrics. Features compared between natural and TTS speech; correlations, PCA, RF importance, and scatter plots reveal MFCC variability and loudness as key predictors.

hyperedges.label: Round 1 TTS Provider Comparison Experiment
hyperedges.description: Round 1 experiment comparing six TTS providers (local 0.6B baseline + five cloud APIs) for voice cloning to drive Ditto lip-sync generation. Evaluated with SyncNet metrics via standard 5-stage pipeline.

nodes.label: Experiments Summary
nodes.content: Comprehensive experiments metrics table for TTS lip-sync quality evaluation. Defines metrics: SyncC (SyncNet Confidence, higher=better), SyncD (SyncNet Distance L2, lower=better), DeltaC (TTS SyncC minus natural), DeltaD (TTS SyncD minus natural). Natural baseline: SyncC=5.632, SyncD=8.189 (n=12). Cross-model comparison of 8 TTS models (Fish S2 Pro, Qwen3-TTS-VC, F5-TTS, Qwen3-TTS-0.6B, CosyVoice2-0.5B, IndexTTS2, GSV-TTS, Higgs TTS 3). IndexTTS2 emotion experiments (8 emotions: angry, calm, surprised, disgusted, happy, afraid, sad, melancholic). Emotion strength experiments (alpha=0.3, 0.6, 1.0). Controlled F5-TTS transform experiments (gain -10dB/+10dB, low-pass 3/6/8kHz, EQ, LUFS loudnorm). Pipeline: TTS synthesis → Ditto animation → SyncNet evaluation. Key finding: simple linear gain +10dB outperforms loudnorm (7.227 vs 7.320 SyncD).

nodes.label: Observational Analysis V2
nodes.content: Statistical analysis of audio feature predictors for SyncNet lip-sync quality. Correlates 52 audio features (MFCC, spectral, energy, pitch) against SyncD and SyncC across 447 scored rows. Top SyncD predictors: mfcc_3_std (Spearman r=-0.3363), mfcc_10_mean (r=-0.2628), mfcc_11_mean (r=-0.2298). Top SyncC predictors: spec_centroid_std (r=-0.3902), onset_mean (r=+0.3486), mfcc_2_mean (r=+0.3107). Includes LASSO regression (R²=0.6028, 43 non-zero features), Random Forest (R²=0.9417), PCA (PC1=25.8%, PC2=18.3%), within-provider partial correlation, loudness normalization effect analysis (LUFS vs original), and provider feature profiles.

nodes.label: Feature vs SyncNet Delta Scatter

Sync-C overall delta: +0.692 (TTS slightly better). Sync-D overall delta: -0.445 (natural better). L0 boundary_sharpness shows TTS advantage in both metrics. Three-tier weight download strategy (hf-mirror.com > proxy > local+SCP). Conda environment management with critical traps: GraalPy resolution, pip upgrade cascades, ONNX Runtime CUDA provider, PyTorch 2.6+ weights_only default. nodes.label: Conda Environment Management

Environment reuse strategy to avoid dependency conflicts.

nodes.label: Weight Download Strategy

nodes.label: Emotion-Aware TTS Synthesis
nodes.content: IndexTTS2 emotion vector inference with 8 emotion categories (angry, calm, surprised, disgusted, happy, afraid, sad, melancholic). Emotion strength controlled by emo_alpha parameter (0.3, 0.6, 1.0). Angry emotion achieves best SyncC (8.109) and SyncD (6.81). Sad/melancholic emotions perform worse than neutral baseline. Higher emo_alpha generally improves SyncD for calm but shows diminishing returns for happy.

nodes.label: Audio Transform Controlled Experiments
nodes.content: Controlled experiments on F5-TTS baseline applying 10 audio transforms (gain, low-pass filtering at 3/6/8kHz, EQ at 1-4kHz ±6dB, LUFS loudnorm). Key findings: simple linear gain +10dB achieves best SyncD (7.227), outperforming loudnorm (7.320). Low-pass 3kHz significantly degrades SyncD (+1.335), confirming >3kHz frequencies are critical for lip-sync. Gain changes show monotonic relationship: louder audio produces better SyncD scores.

nodes.label: Loudness Normalization Effect
nodes.content: Analysis of LUFS-normalized vs original audio within same TTS models (F5-TTS, Higgs TTS 3, ChatTTS, IndexTTS2, GSV-TTS, Fish S2 Pro). Loudnorm to -23 LUFS has inconsistent effects: improves SyncD for F5-TTS (-0.166) and Higgs (-0.280) but degrades it for Fish S2 Pro (+0.890) and IndexTTS2 (+0.236). Dynamic compression (LRA=7, TP=-1) can smooth phoneme boundaries, reducing lip-sync quality.

nodes.label: Audio Feature-SyncNet Correlation
nodes.content: Statistical analysis correlating 52 audio features against SyncD and SyncC. Top SyncD predictors (negative=better): mfcc_3_std (r=-0.3363), mfcc_10_mean (r=-0.2628), mfcc_11_mean (r=-0.2298). Top SyncC predictors: spec_centroid_std (r=-0.3902), onset_mean (r=+0.3486), mfcc_2_mean (r=+0.3107). Random Forest achieves R²=0.9417 with mfcc_3_std as most important feature (0.1016 importance). LASSO selects 43 non-zero features (R²=0.6028).

nodes.label: Phoneme Boundary Sharpness
nodes.content: Analysis of embedding change rate around phoneme boundaries comparing natural and TTS speech. Both show bell-shaped peak at boundary (0ms) with cosine change rate metric. TTS has slightly higher peak (0.2251 vs 0.2118 natural), indicating more abrupt but less smooth transitions in synthesized speech. hyperedges.label: TTS Lip-Sync Evaluation Pipeline
hyperedges.description: End-to-end pipeline for evaluating TTS model lip-sync quality: TTS synthesis produces audio from text+reference → Ditto animation generates talking-face video from portrait+audio → SyncNet evaluation scores SyncC/SyncD confidence and distance metrics. Uses AISHELL-1 test set with 13 speaker portraits.

hyperedges.label: Model-Server Compatibility
hyperedges.description: Compatibility matrix mapping 8 lip-sync models to two GPU servers based on VRAM, CUDA version, and PyTorch constraints. Old server (8×1080 Ti, CUDA 11.4) runs Wav2Lip and MuseTalk. New models require CUDA 12.x and higher VRAM.

hyperedges.label: SyncD Feature Prediction Pipeline
hyperedges.description: Multi-method analysis predicting SyncNet Distance (SyncD) from 52 audio features: Spearman correlation identifies top predictors (mfcc_3_std r=-0.3363), LASSO selects 43 features (R²=0.6028), Random Forest achieves R²=0.9417. Uses 447 scored rows across multiple TTS providers.

hyperedges.label: Wav2Sem Analysis Pipeline (Phase 1)
hyperedges.description: Five-stage Phase 1 pipeline: data assembly → MFA alignment → HuBERT/XLS-R embedding extraction → separability metrics → TFG linkage → report generation

hyperedges.label: Phase 2 Causal Intervention Pipeline
hyperedges.description: Phase 2 causal chain: feature transformations → dose-response → identity control → corrected analysis → stability PGD perturbation. All acoustic mechanisms rejected; G×E co-adaptation and HuBERT stability survive as candidates.

hyperedges.label: TFG Model Comparison Matrix
hyperedges.description: Six-TFG-model comparison using same audio conditions (natural 16kHz vs faster_qwen3 TTS 24kHz) on AISHELL-1 subset, evaluated via SyncNet v2

hyperedges.label: Lip-Sync Model Comparison Pipeline
hyperedges.description: Five lip-sync models deployed across two servers, benchmarked with SyncNet metrics. Wav2Lip ranked best overall; all models show TTS speech improves Sync-C over natural speech.

hyperedges.label: Audio Feature Analysis for Lip-Sync Prediction
hyperedges.description: Multi-figure exploratory analysis of 15+ audio features and their relationship to lip-sync metrics. Features compared between natural and TTS speech; correlations, PCA, RF importance, and scatter plots reveal MFCC variability and loudness as key predictors.

hyperedges.label: Round 1 TTS Provider Comparison Experiment
hyperedges.description: Round 1 experiment comparing six TTS providers (local 0.6B baseline + five cloud APIs) for voice cloning to drive Ditto lip-sync generation. Evaluated with SyncNet metrics via standard 5-stage pipeline.
